resolved.title: 什么是Pandas
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]What is Pandas?[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

[b]Pandas[/b] is one of the most popular data science libraries in Python. Easy to use, it is built on top of [b]NumPy[/b] and shares many functions and properties.

With Pandas, you can read and extract data from files, transform and analyze it, calculate statistics and correlations, and much more! 

To start using pandas, we need to import it first:[code format="py" ]import pandas as pd [/code]
[b]pd[/b] is a common short name used when  importing the library.
[note][b]Pandas[/b] is derived from the term "panel data", an econometrics term for data sets that include observations over multiple time periods for the same individuals.[/note]

resolved.title: Series 和 DataFrame
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Series & DataFrames[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

The two primary components of pandas are the [b]Series[/b] and the [b]DataFrame[/b].

A [b]Series[/b] is essentially a column, and a [b]DataFrame[/b] is a multi-dimensional table made up of a collection of Series.

For example, the following DataFrame is made of two Series, [b]ages[/b] and [b]heights[/b]:[img id="4554" width="60%"]
[note]You can think of a [b]Series[/b] as a one-dimensional array, while a [b]DataFrame[/b] is a multi-dimensional array.[/note]
